title: Apartment Kitchen Ideas: Small, Rental & Galley Upgrades
h1: Apartment Kitchen Ideas: How to Make a Small Rental Kitchen Look High-End
description: Apartment kitchen ideas that work in rentals: renter-safe makeovers, layered lighting, galley layouts, smart storage and decor, with real costs and sizes.
excerpt: Make a small rental kitchen look high-end with reversible upgrades, better lighting, smarter storage and layout-specific ideas for galleys, L-shapes and studios.
image_alt: Small apartment kitchen with clear counters, wood cabinets and a discreet wall cabinet, showing apartment kitchen ideas
key_takeaways: Fix lighting, clutter and dated hardware first; they change a rental kitchen more than any single big purchase.
Match new cabinet pulls to the existing hole spacing (often 3 in. or 96 mm) so you drill no new holes.
Plan roughly 30 to 40 lumens per square foot, with under-cabinet task light mounted toward the front edge.
In a galley, keep the aisle clear (42 in. for one cook) and create a focal point on the end wall.
Keep every original part in a labeled bag and get landlord approval in writing for anything semi-permanent.

faq.q: How can I make my apartment kitchen look better without renovating?
faq.a: Clear the counters down to a few daily-use items grouped on a tray, switch to warm white LED bulbs, add plug-in under-cabinet lights, and replace the cabinet hardware with longer pulls in one finish. Add a washable runner, matching towels and a plant. These changes are reversible, typically cost a few hundred dollars, and make the biggest visible difference.

faq.q: Can I put peel-and-stick backsplash in a rental kitchen?
faq.a: Usually yes, but ask your landlord first and test a small piece for about a week before covering the whole wall. Clean the surface with a degreaser, avoid placing it directly behind a gas burner, and know that adhesive can lift paint on removal. Thicker matte or gel-type tiles look the most convincing.

faq.q: How do you make a galley kitchen look bigger?
faq.a: Keep the floor and aisle clear, use bright under-cabinet lighting on both runs, choose light or glossy backsplash surfaces, and create a focal point on the end wall such as art or a tall shelf. Keeping one side visually quieter than the other also stops a galley feeling like a corridor.

faq.q: What color cabinets make a small kitchen look expensive?
faq.a: Warm whites, soft greige, muted greens and deep navy or charcoal all read as high-end when paired with quality-looking hardware and good lighting. In a rental, removable matte cabinet film or landlord-approved paint can change the color. Repeat one metal finish on hardware and fixtures for a cohesive look.

faq.q: How do I add counter space to a small apartment kitchen?
faq.a: Use a rolling cart with a butcher-block top, an over-the-sink cutting board, a stovetop cover, or a wall-mounted fold-down table. Moving the coffee station to a narrow console nearby also frees the main counter. Choose pieces that roll or fold away when you are not cooking.
